That is the whole risk of the feature — a bug in reading that bit does not produce a broken word run, it produces the Loop 5 marquee vanishing — so `word.spec.ts` drives both from the same hold on the same page.

How the ladder tells the tap detector, in advance, that a stroke is spoken for. `onPolygonPointerUp` scores a tap by travel, and for a hold that measurement is exactly backwards: a long-press that releases where it began has travelled nothing, so it read as a second tap on the ayah already selected — and `App.handleSelect` toggles the selection *off* on a second tap. A reader refining their selection lost it. Called for any latched non-tap intent rather than for `word` alone, because a small marquee had the same shape of bug and a `word`-only guard would be a second place obliged to agree with `nextIntent` about which verdicts are terminal.

One frame of a word stroke: put the point on a word, ink anchor→cursor into the `word` group, and on release say which words those were. The band is drawn with the `"sel"` style over an ayah wash that is still lit — `mix-blend-mode: multiply` is what makes the overlap read as a darker emphasis rather than a second slab, and it is the reason this feature has a golden row at all. `clearWords` is its counterweight: a range and a word run answer different questions about the same page, so only one may be on it.

The only loader keyed by page rather than by surah, because that is how the geometry is stored: a word box is a position on a sheet of paper, so its shard is the sheet. Fetched the moment a hold latches, ~3.6 KB, deliberately not precached — so the first drop into words on a cold page is a round trip, and quiet on a miss: the reader loses the finer grain, not the ayah they had.

extend: `onSelectWords` fires with a `<ayah>#w3-7` key on release — the ayah key with the run appended — and `App.handleSelectWords` is what hears it: `Adjacency.hopsForWords` narrows the edge list to the ones the run is about, and the count is announced. Two rules a second consumer has to keep. The key's indices are the PRINT's — the print↔QAC alignment was applied in ETL and baked into the shards, never here (see `word-indexing`). And the roots must be handed in from `Roots.rootsForWords`, because `Adjacency` holds no root shards: without them a shared-root edge lands in `unplaced` rather than silently passing, which is the honest reading and the reason the refinement returns three outcomes instead of two.

A word run announces its OUTCOME and never its words. «٧ مواضع مشابهة» is the answer the reader dragged for; naming the run would put scripture into a UI string, which is the one thing this grain exists not to do (`docs/design/word-indexing.md` §10 and §11 ②). The overlay stays decorative — `word.spec.ts` asserts the stage's accessibility tree is identical before and after a run — so anything a word run has to say goes through the app's one live region and not through a node on the stage.

The keyboard descent is claimed in the CAPTURE phase on `window`, above the highlighter's own bubble-phase listener on the SVG: `Enter` on an already-selected ayah descends, `←`/`→` carry the run, `Shift` extends it, `Escape` climbs one rung. That ordering is the whole mechanism — it needs no L1 change, and it is why the arrows do not fall through to the page-turner. `word.spec.ts` proves the page did not turn by reading the slider's `aria-valuetext`, because a page that turned and a page that never loaded look identical in the SVG.

The e2e nudge is not decoration. `filterTaps: true` gives @use-gesture's drag a 3 px threshold, so a hold that moves 1 px produces no frame and the ladder is never consulted — a spec that presses and waits will watch the feature do nothing. Both `word.spec.ts` and the golden row carry `NUDGE_PX` and say why.

A golden that photographs a *gesture* must aim with the paint, not with a bounding box: the golden row takes the widest selection band because it is a whole line of print with both ends known, and aiming by box put the press 12 px from the window edge with the run growing off-screen.

features.what: The ETL as one shape, rather than fourteen scripts each documented where it lives: what runs, in what order, which of the 23 gates fences which edge, and where the wall between text and numbers sits. The orientation page you read BEFORE adding a build script, a gate or a corpus — every specific it names is owned by another document, and it links there rather than restating.

entry.symbol: Seven vendored inputs, seven writers, six shard trees
entry.note: Five diagrams: the spine, the four encodings and the three joins between them, the gates overlaid on the spine, the one-way text boundary, and the seven scripts that build nothing. Every number in it is quoted from a pin file and the pin file is named beside it — 91,451 boxes from word-boxes.pin.json, 86,965 → 77,429 words from word-alignment.pin.json, 60,057 annotations from tajweed-words.probe.json.

The ordinary path, and what it deliberately omits. build-words.mjs and build-alignment.mjs are NOT in this chain because both read the gitignored ligature cache, so chaining them would make the ordinary build fail on a clean checkout. Their outputs are committed and gate:words / gate:align re-derive them from committed bytes instead — the trick that lets a cache-dependent build be checked offline.

The 380 MB that is a source and never a shard. Per-word SVG for all 604 pages, gitignored, and the only things that leave it are numbers — box geometry and a word index. It is the single reason the four probes cannot be gates, and the reason diagram ④ of the design doc reads the way it does: text may enter memory, only arithmetic may be written.

The 23, in the order `make ci` runs them. Diagram ③ overlays this list on the spine so it is visible which edge each gate guards — and that three of them (gate:edges, gate:gates, gate:ci-artifacts) exist because something shipped broken between two checks that both passed.

A report, not a gate, and the distinction is historical rather than stylistic: it was written when 3 of 604 pages were vendored and had to keep working through the gap, so it REPORTS a missing page. gate:pages is what fails on one now. Kept because describing the corpus and policing it are different jobs and this one still does the first.

The only output of this pipeline whose consumer is a person. Seeded so a round can be re-run, stratified so the rare edge classes gate:edges cannot score are not invisible, deduped to unordered pairs because the scarcest input this project has is a human minute with a mus'haf open.

extend: Add a script to packages/etl/scripts/ and it must appear in at least one diagram here. That rule is the whole of what keeps this page honest — see `etl-map-should-generate-itself` in docs/issues.json for why it is a rule a human follows rather than a gate, and what evidence would overturn that.

Numbers in this document are quoted, never computed here. Every figure carries the pin file it came from, so a moved measurement shows up as a diff in the pin and a stale sentence here is findable by grepping for the number. Do not write a figure whose source you cannot name.

Do not restate. Provenance lives in each corpus's PROVENANCE.md, licences in SOURCES.md, the two hard joins in word-indexing.md and encoding-inspector.md. This page owns the SHAPE — order, ownership, and which check covers which edge — and nothing else.

A new gate goes in three places (`pnpm gates`, `make ci`, the workflow) or gate:gates fails, and then in diagram ③ so a reader can see what it fences. A gate that guards nothing visible on the spine is a sign the spine drawing is wrong, not that the diagram should be skipped.

Change a figure here and a dozen of them are also copied into a public post in another repository — see §⑧ for which ones and why nothing enforces the copy. Nothing can: the two repos share no CI and neither build may depend on the other's checkout or on the network, which is the same constraint that made four of this pipeline's own measurements probes rather than gates. Update the post in the same change, or leave it correct about an older measurement, which is what its date already claims.

features.what: Turning the mutashabihat dataset into the per-surah shards the app hops through.

entry.note: Dataset + curated edges → 114 shards. Reverse edges are generated here, so an edge stated once is navigable from both ends.
The 6236-ayah numbering the datasets speak, and its inverse. Every off-by-one bug in this project has lived within one function of this pair.

The +1 that bridges a 0-based dataset to a 1-based core. It shipped missing, and 47.8% of the hop corpus pointed at an ayah sharing no words with its source — a mutashabihat instrument being quietly, entirely wrong. Nothing caught it: the curated Loop-2 edges are written as "S:A" strings and skip this conversion, so every gate and every e2e stayed green over the only edges anyone had looked at. The comment above it carries the measurement; read it before touching numbering here.

The gate that would have caught the off-by-one on day one. Every dataset-derived edge is scored by the longest contiguous run of words its two ends share, and CI fails past 10% of them sharing none. Random ayah pairs score 69% there, the broken corpus scored 48%, the corrected one 3.9% — the threshold sits in a gap, not on a tuning knob.

The one reader of the vendored morphology, and the one definition of 'how similar are these two ayahs'. The gate enforces a floor on this number and the sampler prints it beside each pair a human audits — computed a second time, they would eventually disagree, and the human would be the one assumed wrong.

The spot-audit draw. Stratified by type × provenance × page distance, because 97% of the pairs are one class and a flat draw of twenty never shows the classes gate:edges cannot reach. The unit is the unordered pair, not the directed edge — the corpus generates both directions from one fact, so asking a reader about both spends the scarcest input this project has on a question already answered.

extend: Vendoring a new dataset: add the SOURCES.md entry with its licence in the same commit as the data. gate:license fails otherwise, deliberately.
Every script prints a summary line — counts in, counts out, largest shard. Read it; a silent 10% drop in edges looks exactly like success.
Human verdicts on specific edges are permanent. They go in the verified-edges register, and gate:verified-edges enforces them from then on.

Data here can be structurally perfect and semantically noise; gate:edges is the only check that reads meaning. A new edge type whose promise is shared phrasing belongs in its SCORED_TYPES, or it ships unmeasured.
A new edge type also becomes a new stratum in the spot-audit draw automatically, and `make validate` will show it as a class nobody has looked at until someone does.

features.what: What the reader has opened, by day and by page, hizb or juz — the log, and the picture drawn from it. Never leaves the device.

entry.note: Start here, and read the doc comment before the fields. It enumerates what must NOT become an event — a toggle-off, a hop arrival, a share-link arrival — because recording those evenly maps app usage rather than revision, and the two diverge exactly where the record was meant to be useful. The `tz` field rides on the event rather than being passed at read time: a single offset applied at display time re-files every look recorded on the other side of a DST change or a flight.

Scopes are `page`, `hizb` and `juz`. A page yields exactly one id; a hizb or a juz can straddle, and then the event credits both. Unparseable input yields `[]`, so a corrupt record is a gap in the picture rather than a wrong colour. `hizb` only exists here because HIZB_STARTS is vendored — the tempting derivation, half a juz, is wrong, and a scope whose boundaries are guessed is a heatmap that lies about which ayahs it is colouring.

The only impure half: the one place that reads a clock and touches storage, and therefore the one place that can lie. Note that opening the store stamps `since` — iOS deletes script-writable storage after seven days of no interaction, so the record has to know how young it is or an emptied log reads as «you have revised nothing».

Retention, run once per calendar day from both the write path and the read path. A boolean got this wrong: a session left open across midnight never pruned again, and a read-only session — open the app, look, close — never pruned at all and handed the picture rows the store had promised to have forgotten.

The two honest signals, and the whole wiring: a tap inside the `!toggledOff` branch, and a marquee release as one event carrying both ends. `handleHop` and the hash router set the selection past `handleSelect` on purpose, which is what makes the three exclusions hold by construction rather than by discipline.

A log of when someone was reading Qur'an is not a preference. This is a closed allow-list of modules permitted to import the record, plus a grep for escape hatches inside the record's own files. Deliberately not `import/no-restricted-paths`, which expresses the inverse rule and would leave every new URL-building file unguarded by default.

The picture's half of the honesty problem: when 3 of 604 pages were vendored, a division the reader could not reach had to not be drawn as one they neglected — absent is no fill and a dashed hairline, cold is the sunk paper, and the two differ in kind rather than in opacity. `holdings` answers that by pushing every vendored ayah through the same `scopesOf` the record uses, so «absent» and «warm» cannot drift about which hizb a page is in. It was `coverage` and returned a set; it returns a map now, because the same sweep that says «is there paper here» can say «and the lowest page of it we hold» for free, and that number is where a press on the cell lands (`docs/design/revision-record.md` ②). Lowest, not first-encountered: nothing in `PageMeta` promises the manifest is ascending. Read off the manifest and never off `HIZB_STARTS`, which knows which *ayah* opens a hizb but not which page of *this* build prints it — a landing the build cannot show is unrepresentable rather than a case to remember. The sheet opens from the page chip, not a sixth header button: `e2e/chrome-fit` holds the row inside 320px with seventeen pixels to spare.

entry.symbol: a tap on an ayah is still on the map after a reload
entry.note: The only test that can prove a tap became durable: the unit suite hands the component a record, and a store that wrote to memory would pass all of it. Note `recorded()` — the write is fired and forgotten from the tap handler, so a reload can outrun it; and it must be `expect.poll` over `evaluate`, because `waitForFunction`'s poller does not await a promise and would succeed on the first tick regardless of what the database holds.

entry.symbol: credits the source of a hop, never the ayah the app moved them to
entry.note: The three exclusions asserted end to end through the real UI. `revision.test.ts` and `revision-store.test.ts` can prove what a look is worth; only this file can prove App.tsx does not call `recordLook` from the three places it must not.

The boundaries a per-hizb heatmap will be labelled with — sixty vendored [surah, ayah] pairs, not thirty juz halved. Tanzil publishes no hizb element at all: the division is 240 quarters and a hizb is four of them. The shortcut agrees for 4 of 30 and misses by up to 39 ayahs, which is the whole reason this is a table.

What keeps the tables honest: AYAH_COUNTS, JUZ_STARTS and HIZB_STARTS are re-derived from packages/etl/data/meta/quran-data.xml on every CI run and diffed. The last check is the interesting one — if more than 4 of 30 even hizbs sit on their juz's midpoint, someone regenerated the table by halving, and the gate says so by name instead of letting sixty plausible numbers through.

extend: Anything that reads the record is a new importer: add it to ALLOWED_IMPORTERS in the gate with a one-line reason. If it cannot state a reason it cannot see the record.

Adding a scope means adding real boundary data first. `hizb` was the standing example and is now the worked one: the arithmetic derivation is wrong, so the sixty starts are vendored from the Tanzil metadata and `gate:quran-meta` re-derives them on every run. A scope whose boundaries are guessed is a heatmap that lies about which ayahs it is colouring, and no other test here would notice.

New callers of `recordLook` must justify themselves against the `RevisionEvent` doc comment. The default answer is no: the record is only worth drawing because it is not a log of everything that happened.

The warmth bands (2/7/30 days in RevisionMap.tsx) are a developer's guess and are named as one in docs/design/revision-record.md. Changing them wants a hafiz, not an argument. What is not negotiable is the axis: recency, which is why `lastSeen` exists apart from `rollUp`.

The map is a way in, not only a picture: a held cell is a `<button>` that opens its division, an absent cell stays a plain `<li>` with nothing to press, and the whole 604-cell grid is one tab stop (a roving `tabindex`, arrows stepping over the paper we do not have). New cells inherit that shape — a control that refuses is worse than an outline that never offered, and 604 tab stops inside a Tab-trapped dialog is a map nobody can leave. Note `focusables()` here is no longer Colophon's verbatim copy: it excludes `tabindex="-1"`, or the trap's `last` element lands in the middle of the grid.

Navigation from the map deliberately does not write to the record: `recordLook` is called only from the two honest signals in App.tsx, so pressing a cell cannot warm the cell you just pressed. A page-turn added anywhere else must keep that property, or the picture starts drawing the reader looking at it.

Loop 4b vendored the other 601 pages and the map itself needed nothing — `holdings` reads the manifest — but the e2e did, exactly as predicted: it had pinned hizb 3 as the first division with no paper and the inventory as «المتوفّر ٢ من ٦٠ حزب», and both failed loudly. It is «٦٠ من ٦٠» now, and «absent is not cold» is held by a second row that trims pages 22–31 out of the manifest. Keep that row: with a complete edition the absent treatment has no way to appear on its own, and it is what the map owes the next edition that does not carry the whole print.

features.what: Usable by someone who cannot see the page: labels on the polygons, a live region for what changed, and Arabic digits everywhere.

entry.note: Where an invisible polygon becomes a focusable, labelled control. If a new drawn thing should be reachable by screen reader or keyboard, it happens here.
One aria-live region for the whole app. Several would race and interrupt each other.

Every number a user hears or reads, in the digits their UI language reads them in — `toArabicDigits` beneath it is the Arabic half. The bug this prevents is a badge showing ٣ while the label says 'three'; invisible until an aria snapshot puts the two side by side. The `lang` parameter is required on purpose: a default would let a new call site render Arabic-Indic digits inside an English sentence and still compile.

The accessible tree, committed as text under e2e/__aria__/. Snapshots are text, not geometry, so they are keyed by project and not by platform — a Linux runner and a Mac must produce the same tree or one of them is wrong.

extend: Any new control: a label in Arabic, a 44px target, and a visible focus ring. The contrast spec checks the third and will fail you.

Numbers in user-facing strings go through `digits(n, lang)` — including inside aria-labels, which is the half everyone forgets. Never `String(n)`, and never `toArabicDigits` directly: one is wrong in Arabic and the other is wrong in English.
Update the aria snapshots deliberately (`--update-snapshots`) and read the diff. An accepted snapshot is the only place a broken tree can hide.

features.what: The visual gate: highlight geometry the DOM cannot describe, pinned as images.

entry.note: Golden images are keyed by {platform} because they are rasterized geometry. The aria snapshots beside them are keyed by {projectName} because they are text — mixing the two axes is a bug in both directions.

The pinned container. The generator and the checker must be the same rasterizer or the gate is a coin flip; gate:golden-env enforces that the Makefile, the CI job, and the installed Playwright all agree.
Why the baselines are committed to git rather than LFS, and the number at which that answer should be revisited.

Which pages are photographed and *why each one*. Five pages chosen as five geometry classes, not five pages: 1 is the only viewBox override class (235×235, so the only width-bound fit) and the page gate:pages skips by name; 7/9/19 are the original three, mid-surah, varying in density; 604 is the only page with surah header bands on it. A shot that duplicates another's coverage is pure cost, so the docblock states each page's job and the reader is expected to add to it.

extend: Adding a row means adding baselines for BOTH platforms: `make golden-update` for darwin, `make golden-linux UPDATE=1` for linux.

Pick a page for a geometry class, not for variety: say in the SHOTS docblock what this page can fail at that no existing shot can see. If that sentence cannot be written, the shot is cost without coverage.
Open the changed PNGs before committing. An accepted baseline is the gate agreeing with you, which is worth nothing unless you looked.
Never bump Playwright without bumping GOLDEN_IMAGE and re-rendering — the failure mode is ten red diffs that look exactly like a UI regression.

features.what: The checks a machine cannot do — a phone in a hand, a mushaf on a table — tracked so they cannot quietly not happen.

entry.note: The only place a manual runbook is written. `make validate CHECK=<id>` prints it, `make guide` renders it for a phone, the /validate skill drives it.
Does NOT fail on outstanding checks — a phone that has not been held is a fact, not a broken build. It fails when the ledger lies.
Writes the verdict back and then prints what that verdict now obliges — the standing rule is that a manual result must tighten something automated.

The only writer of docs/validation/evidence/. Runs each check's declared `evidence.run` and writes the real exit code; everything else only reads. Exits 0 even when a producer goes red — a reporting run, not a gate.
Exit 3 is "could not tell", and it is not a pass — so a producer that could not reach its subject strikes no step off a human's runbook.
Derived from the check id, never stored beside it: a path written down in two places is a path that can disagree with itself.

One renderer for a check, shared by the field guide and the session page, so a runbook step cannot read one way on the phone and another on the laptop. `capture` is the only difference between the two surfaces — it stamps each step with its ledger id as well as its position, the same rule `evidence.covers` lives under, so a reordered runbook cannot silently re-point a transcript.

The writing surface: one check, served to the phone, every tick and note appended to a transcript as it happens rather than typed from memory at the end. This is the opt-in a check's own tool gets — inject a sink, and a page built for the check posts to it; opened as a plain file it finds nothing and keeps its offline behaviour. `--tool <path>` overrides the page the ledger pins, which is what lets a check whose population was cut into sixteen parts serve any of them through the sink instead of off a static file server; the transcript records which page it was opened against. Every /api route is token-gated because the server binds 0.0.0.0 for the phone, and these files are treated as evidence.

Arithmetic only — counts, the notes in order, the last verdict — and deliberately never a score. placement-correction-by-eye is a blind forced choice whose validity rests on nobody, the worker included, knowing how it is going while it is going; a progress bar is fine, a running tally would turn the measurement into a training exercise.

The one part of edge-spot-audit a machine can reach: a second opinion on the print, fetched rather than held. api.quran.com publishes a V1/1405H page table and ours is V2/1421H, so the two must disagree on exactly 36 pages — which turns a useless source into a fingerprint, and makes agreement where they should differ as much a finding as the reverse. `probe-` and not `gate-` because it reaches the network, same reasoning as check-source-offer.mjs. Keys only, no `fields`, so no Quran text crosses the wire.

The prose half of the probe: which published references are reachable (measured), what each can and cannot settle, and the trap — six of archive.org's twelve KFGQPC scans are a different qira'a or script, so comparing against one produces confident, wrong verdicts. The symbol is the frontmatter name and not a section heading because scripts/code-pointers.mjs reads a leading `#` as a comment, so no Markdown heading can ever be a live pointer; the name is the better anchor anyway, since renaming the skill is the change that would actually strand this row.

extend: A new manual check is a ledger entry with a full runbook. A pending user-owned check with no steps fails the gate, because a check nobody can follow will not be run.
Edit the ledger and re-run `make guide` in the same commit — a staleness hash fails the build otherwise.
When a check comes back, record it and then do what `tunes` printed. That step is what turns a verdict into a permanent test instead of a note.

An `evidence` block must name a `residue` — say in words what the command cannot do. The gate rejects one that does not, because an automated run naming no remainder is one claiming to have done a human's job.

`evidence.covers` points at runbook step ids, never positions, and `evidence.run` is a script rather than a make target — make flattens every failed recipe to exit 2, which would let a network timeout read as a verdict.

A check whose work is a purpose-built page declares it as `runbook.tool` and the page opts into `window.HIFTH_SESSION` — never send that sink anything the page is not supposed to know. The adjudication tool posts which panel was chosen and never whether it was right, because the answer key does not exist until the scorer rebuilds it from the seed.

Before asking a human for a mushaf, run `make probe-reference ALL=1` and see what is left. It cannot judge whether two ayahs resemble each other — nothing on a network can — but it settles every arithmetic claim underneath that question, and it must never become a gate: a check that reaches the internet teaches everyone to skip it the first time a host is down.

features.what: Every question this project has had to answer, in words a person outside the repo can act on.

entry.note: The register. Fifteen records already existed in docs/decisions/ with no way in: their titles are sentences — 'The grain gets finer where the finger already is' is a good title and a useless index entry — so a reader arriving with a question could not find which file answers it. The running-table habit existed and was scoped to one topic (desktop-vs-mobile.md says 'append a row there rather than restating one here') and nothing generalised it, so an open decision could sit in a design doc's eighth section for a month with nothing counting it as open. Stores exactly one sentence of its own, the plain-language `question`, and points at the record for everything else — same anti-duplication rule as issues.json and the ledger. The exception is `related`, which is not a restatement of anything: relatedness is a property of a PAIR, so no single record can hold it, and the second half of a pair is normally written months after the first — by which time the first is not the file anybody opens. Hand-edited, never generated.

The half that is easy to skip: who a decision is FOR. An open decision must carry both an `artifact` — the published page anybody can open — and a `page`, the same picture checked in here, and the gate fails on either alone. A link with no copy dies when the host does; a copy with no link cannot be sent to anyone. Whatever is checked in names the script that rebuilds it, because a committed page nobody can regenerate is a screenshot with extra steps that starts lying the day the data moves. And the record has to link to both, or its argument is about a picture the reader cannot reach. Also carries the reverse check issues.json exists for: a record in docs/decisions/ with no row here. And `related` must be symmetric: naming a decision that does not name you back is a link invisible from the end a reader is usually standing at.

The CLAUDE.md tenet, in characters — the only place it is more than a preference. Refuses a question or an option label that names a file, a path, a symbol, a command, a gate, or backticked code, because each of those makes a reader look something up before they can have an opinion. Deliberately does NOT check reading age, sentence length or word difficulty: those are taste, and a gate that enforces taste gets switched off. Domain words — verse, tajweed, madd, ghunnah, mus'haf — pass, and should: translating them out makes the page vaguer, not simpler.

Renders docs/decisions/README.md, open first. Every title is read out of the record at build time and none is stored — the register holds the question, the record owns the answer, and a title living in two files is right for a while and then quietly stops being right. Stamped with a hash the gate compares, the same rule as issues.md and the validation guide.

Scoped to the staged files, silent when a commit touches none of them. This pairing breaks on exactly one kind of commit — the one that adds the artifact link before committing the page, or renames the page and leaves the link — and that is the commit where the information is free, because you are moving the thing right now.

The rule applied, as a checklist: question-shaped headings, no identifiers in prose a reader must follow, a glossary for the domain words, every option drawn on real data at the size it would really be used, and what the page does NOT settle stated on the page. Not a template — the shape of an options page follows the question; what does not vary is that a reader can follow it cold. The symbol is the frontmatter name for the reason mushaf-reference gives: code-pointers.mjs reads a leading `#` as a comment, so no heading can be a live pointer.

The worked example of what the skill asks for, and of the split every options generator wants: `--extract` reads the 348 MB gitignored page cache and writes a small JSON of findings; the default render reads only committed bytes, so the page rebuilds on a fresh clone. `--artifact` re-renders it with the print inlined once as a <symbol> and <use>d per specimen — the publishing host blocks every external request, so a relative URL does not error, it silently draws nothing, and six data: URIs would be six copies of 64 KB. That copy is gitignored: same page, roughly twice the bytes.

The second options page, and the one that shows what a generator is FOR: its central claim is one nobody can make in a paragraph — that eighteen editable colours do not fit on cream paper — so it builds the best honest eighteen it can, fanning each family's hue in lightness and a little in hue, and then counts what that costs. Answer: **18 pairs closer together than the closest pair in today's seven**, which is the argument against option C, generated rather than asserted, and it would move on its own if the palette moved. Deliberately shares build-mark-options.mjs's stylesheet verbatim — the two pages are the same kind of document about the same seven colours, a reader will arrive at one from the other, and two option pages that do not look like siblings read as two projects. Unlike its sibling it has NO `--extract` half: every number comes from the shipped shards, `rules.json`, `tokens.css` and `skins.ts`, so there is nothing to stale. The two measurements the record turns on are computed here and nowhere else: `shown` — the share of a rule's own ayahs in which its family ALSO won the ayah's single tint, 1.6% for the commonest madd — and `ambiguous`, the 620 ayahs (10.0%) whose winning family is carried by more than one rule, where an eighteen-colour palette has no non-arbitrary answer at all. `--artifact` emits the body only, without a document shell: the publishing host wraps what it is given, and a second <html> inside the first is discarded along with the <style> it was carrying.

The third options page, and the one where the drawing does work no table can: the decision is about a displacement of roughly one unit on a mark 5.6 by 3.6, which is a number in a column and an obvious error in a picture. Every option is drawn twice on page 179 — a band of three printed lines at about phone size, and a ten-times close-up on the mark that option moves furthest — with `layerInk` drawing the measured truth as a dashed outline beside the filled box, so the reader sees the gap shrink from A to I rather than being told it does. Page 179 is chosen by measurement, not by eye: its four rungs (98.7 / 16.0 / 7.8 / 3.4%) sit at the corpus median on every one, and the footer says so, because an options page that quietly picked its best page is an advert. The letters are the RECORD's — A, B, F, G, I, H — not this page's own; numbering them A–F would have given one option two names depending on which document a reader opened, and C, D and E stay in the record where §⑩ names them. The ORDER is not the letters' order: I sits beside F because the two differ by one thing and the board's severity bar should collapse along the reader's eye, and H goes last because its number is not measured the way the others' are. The board's `grid-template-columns` is written by the builder from `OPTIONS.length` (7rem plus 50rem shared out) rather than hard-coded, because a hard-coded five silently pushed a sixth option behind a horizontal scroll nobody drags; the stylesheet keeps an `auto-fit` fallback for the same reason. Two crop rules were found by looking rather than reasoning and are load-bearing: the band is measured off its own boxes and cut through the white space between printed lines (a word box is as tall as its line, so a tight crop lets the neighbour lean in), and the close-up only considers marks at least half its window from either page edge, or it lands half off the paper. Every figure is the held-out half — fitted on one half of each page's marks, scored on the other — and the score is the residual against the same per-mark displacements the dashed outlines are drawn at. `--extract` needs the gitignored cache and a rows file; the render needs only committed bytes. Sibling stylesheet to build-mark-options.mjs, for the reason recorded there.

extend: A new decision is a record in docs/decisions/ (or a section of the design doc that owns it), a row in docs/decisions.json, and `make decisions-doc`. The gate refuses a record with no row, which is the direction nothing else checks.
Write the question in plain words or the build says so. No file names, no symbols, no commands — the record's body is where those belong. See CLAUDE.md for why this is a tenet and not a style note.
An open decision needs two or more options and something to look at, published AND checked in. If there is nothing to look at yet, the decision is not open, it is unstarted.
Never paraphrase a decision into the register. It stores the question; the record owns the answer, and `make decisions` reads the answer out of the record as you run it.

Legible is not answerable. A page that opens with three options gives a reader the last thing they need first — so the record and the page both say why it is being asked now, what happens if nobody decides, what people outside this project already do (linked; and if you did not look, say so), what we have already decided that constrains it, what was left off the option list and why, and what would change the answer. The decide skill is that list in full.
Fill `related` in BOTH rows. One direction resolves fine and reads as complete, which is why it is the failure worth a gate.
When the call is made, set `decided`, `by` and `date` — and leave the losing options on the page. They are the reason the choice was a choice, and the next person to reopen it will want them.

features.what: Every glyph on screen traces to a named source under a named licence, and the offer to hand that source over resolves.

entry.note: The register of everything vendored. Not documentation — two gates parse it, so an entry is a load-bearing part of the build.
Fails if something is vendored without a recorded licence. The obligation is legal, so the check is mechanical.
What the user is actually told. Not authored here — each row is declared in its SOURCES.md ```colophon fence and this renders it, so the record and the screen cannot drift.
Enforces that binding, and refuses a non-commercial claim nobody recorded — the exact defect that once told every reader the KFGQPC artwork was more restricted than it is.
Where the offer points. It has to actually resolve for a stranger — that is a real obligation, not a nice-to-have.

The offer, followed the way a stranger would follow it: anonymously, no gh and no token, because signed in as ourselves a private repo looks public. Named `check-` and not `gate-` because it reaches the public internet and is deliberately not in `pnpm gates` — it runs on demand (`make source-offer`) and from the public-deploy workflow.

entry.symbol: Android is reachable and the App Store is the blocked one
entry.note: Where the vendored licences stop being paperwork and start deciding a roadmap. Every gate above satisfies the obligations of a static site, where the browser is handed the whole bundle and GPL §4–6 are discharged by construction; none of them says anything about a store binary, which is a different distribution under the same licences. The doc is the argument that Track B's stated order is not achievable, and §⑦ ② is honest that a non-lawyer reading licence text is not the standard `gate:*` holds everything else to.

extend: Vendor nothing without its SOURCES.md entry in the same commit.
To change what the reader is told about a licence, edit that source's ```colophon fence in SOURCES.md. The component follows; gate:license-copy fails if it does not.
A source the app should not credit still has to say so — `not-credited: <reason>` in the fence. Silence is indistinguishable from an oversight, which is why it is not allowed.
A GPL-derived asset makes this repo the corresponding source. That constrains unrelated decisions, including whether binaries can live behind a metered service (see gate:golden-size).

features.what: What judges a change, and the rule that every gate is reproducible locally.

entry.note: An exact mirror of the build-test-gate job, in CI order. If you add a step to one, add it to the other in the same commit — that promise is the whole value of the target.
Four jobs: secrets-scan, build-test-gate, e2e (containerised), lighthouse. Only the second is what `make ci` mirrors; the other three have their own make targets.

The `extend` rule below, enforced. Every gate:* script in package.json must be invoked by `pnpm gates`, by the Makefile ci target, and by a workflow job — and every gate named in those three must exist. Written after the rule was broken twice in prose-only form: gate:pages was merged wired to nothing at all, and gate:edges ran in `make ci` but in no job, which is the worse direction because the author sees a pass the branch protection never saw. Three places to remember is two too many; memory is not a mechanism. No exemption list, deliberately — a gate that genuinely cannot run in CI is a conversation, not an array entry.
Every artifact CI uploads is one something actually produces. Written after an upload step preserved nothing for several loops while looking green.

Where Loop 4b's `< 2.5 s TTI on mid-Android` is actually evaluated. The four `categories:*` assertions cannot do it: Lighthouse 12 gives the TTI audit weight 0 in the `hidden` group, so a perfect 100 on performance promises nothing about it. The emulated device is written out in `collect.settings` rather than inherited from Lighthouse's default preset — inherited, an upgrade that retunes the preset would silently change which phone the criterion is about. Median of five runs, because the metric steps rather than scatters: it moves in whole `rttMs` units as the LCP resource lands one simulated round trip later or earlier.

The 150 KB budget notices at the cliff; scripts/budget-baseline.json is how it notices on the slope. Every run prints a per-chunk delta and fails on a move of more than a kilobyte in either direction — a shrink too, because unrecorded headroom is headroom the next change spends unseen. The baseline is committed rather than built from main because that puts the number in the diff a reviewer is already reading instead of a CI log nobody opens, and because a merge-base build cannot run offline. Accept a move with `make budget-update`, and read the diff — an accepted baseline is the gate agreeing with you.
This map, checked. Every symbol listed in docs/map.json must still exist, so the orientation doc cannot rot into confident fiction.

The promises, checked. docs/use-cases.json names the test behind each thing this app claims to do; this asserts those tests still exist and are still tests. Rename a test and the commit doing it is told which promise it was standing behind.

extend: A new gate is a script in scripts/, a `gate:*` entry in package.json, a link in the `gates` composite, a line in `make ci`, and a step in build-test-gate. All five, or it does not run — and gate:gates now says so out loud instead of leaving it to this sentence, which was written first and then broken twice.
Verify a new gate by breaking the thing it protects and watching it fail, then reverting. A gate that has never failed has never been tested.
Gates fail with the fix in the message. 'X is wrong' costs someone an afternoon; 'X is wrong, run Y' costs them a minute.

A gate that guards a number with headroom needs a committed baseline as well as a ceiling, or it only speaks on the change that runs out. gate:budget is the shape: measure, commit the measurement, fail on drift, and let the baseline's diff be the report — the same trade the golden images make.
